CS-H-01.note: Key uniquely correct: 'written in a single hand and a single ink over a span of a few days, drawing on loose slips ... discarded once the fair season had closed' fixes both halves of 'retrospective compilations'. Closest miss is 'unofficial abstracts' (the books ARE condensed from slips), but 'unofficial' is defeated by 'the guild's officers had settled their accounts' in the same clause. Medium not hard: the blank is pre-cued by the opening contrast with 'day-by-day records', so 'retrospective' is reachable before the evidence sentence.

CS-H-02.note: Checked hard per instruction. 'Accommodation' survives most of the passage (mutual adjustment) and is only defeated by 'on terms that neither fixes for long' - an accommodation names a settlement reached, a negotiation names terms still in motion; the transactional cycle (service, theft, sanction, an unusually gentle service to win the client back) is bargaining, which 'accommodation' does not carry. It is one clause of separation and it holds, but this is the tightest key in the batch and it is the item to watch if students split. 'Ongoing' in the stem weakens the defeat slightly by pre-supplying the unfixed sense. Genuinely hard on the stated definition.

CS-H-03.note: 'The language was inserted to deprive that council of any pretext for refusal' is a direct statement of defensive purpose. 'A political concession' would require yielding, and the minutes show withholding; 'a genuine prediction' is the reading the passage exists to overturn; 'a technical oversight' is contradicted by 'inserted'. One inference, three flat distractors.

CS-H-04.note: Key is right and unique - 'attaches to the configurations that games produce rather than to boards as such' is the definition of a specialized memory. But the flagged concern is real and it is an option-family tell, not a key defect: efficient / deliberate / resilient are three generic cognitive virtues and 'specialized' is the only word naming a domain restriction, so the odd-one-out is pickable with the passage covered. passage_needed false on that basis. Fix by making at least one distractor domain-shaped (e.g. 'pattern-driven', 'configural') rather than a virtue.

CS-H-05.note: 'which of them happened to reach the burned ground before the others' supplies 'accidental' almost lexically. 'Predictable' is the overturned reading and 'gradual' is contradicted by 'within the first three years'. Reachable by any student who reads the last clause.

CS-H-06.note: Checked hard per instruction. The key is 'faithful' and 'literal' is cleanly defeated by a structural constraint, not a shade of meaning: the blank must name a promise that readers WRONGLY believe was broken ('The complaint mistakes the promise'). If the preface had promised 'literal', the complaint would be correct, not mistaken. 'Faithful' is the only option with the two-sense ambiguity the passage needs - fidelity to surface vs to argument. 'Exacting' fails the same test and is odd English of a version; 'idiomatic' is satisfied by the rendering readers object to, so no complaint would arise. Best-built item in the batch and hard on the stated definition: a defensible-looking distractor settled only by a second feature.

CS-H-07.note: Mechanism is spelled out to the point of paraphrase ('each intrusion of water leaves the block knitted where it had been weakest'). Same option-family shape as CS-H-04: three static properties (inert, dense, internally redundant) against one dynamic process word, so 'self-repairing' is the odd one out with the passage covered. passage_needed false.

CS-H-08.note: Checked hard per instruction. The qualified endorsement is what makes it work rather than what breaks it. 'A lapse in judgment' is the live trap because the supporting clause ('no one had asked for the tables, and they made the thinness of the sample plain') reads more naturally as evidence of a blunder than of candor - but 'and in a sense it was' cannot be true of a lapse once the closing sentence shows the appendix was calculated, whereas candor survives a self-interested motive. Two features settle it, in the right order. Genuinely hard.

CS-H-09.note: Key unique; B is a real near-miss because the quoted sentence belongs to the ash test, but it reports the outcome, not the method. QUOTED-STEM DEFECT: stem lifts 70 characters ('The ash dates matched the layer counts in each core to within a decade'). The quoted span alone is enough - 'matched ... to within a decade' marks it as a result, and only one option says 'reports a test result'. Answerable without the rest of the passage.

CS-H-10.note: Key unique; C (the misdirection conclusion) belongs to the closing sentence and is the only live competitor. QUOTED-STEM DEFECT and the worst case in the batch: the stem is 214 characters and lifts 131 of them verbatim. From the quote alone, 'Pigment analysis has since shown' marks it as a finding, which eliminates the assumption option and the conclusion option; a solver reaches D without the passage.

CS-H-11.note: B is the intended trap and is cleanly defeated by 'complicated the sequence rather than the climate' plus 'Nobody disputes the drought' - but the text states the defeat outright rather than leaving it to inference, so medium. Short stem, no quoted span; structurally the cleanest of the structure items.

CS-H-12.note: 'shows instead' in the next sentence marks the displacement explicitly, and the three distractors each summarize an adjacent sentence. QUOTED-STEM DEFECT: 81 characters lifted. The quoted span carries the phrase 'The obvious inference was', which by itself names the function (an explanation about to be replaced) - fully answerable from the stem.

CS-H-13.note: The target sentence opens 'A single interpretation now covers both results', which is the key restated. Distractors are three flat adjacent-sentence summaries. No quoted span, but no difficulty either.

CS-H-14.note: Key unique by elimination - B, C and D each summarize a different sentence. Mild wording risk: the listeners 'reported no change they could agree on', which is a report of disagreement rather than of no change, so 'corroborates the listeners' reports' is slightly generous; no other option is defensible, so it does not threaten the key. QUOTED-STEM DEFECT: 104 characters lifted, and the quote contains both 'Measurements' and 'the instruments' own tolerance', which hands over the only option mentioning evidence that 'does not depend on their judgment'. Answerable from the stem.

CS-H-15.note: Key unique; D (the misapplied-protocol conclusion) is the only competitor and belongs to the final sentence. QUOTED-STEM DEFECT: 62 characters lifted ('The tests, however, are conducted at a constant twenty degrees'). The quote is self-identifying as a feature of the testing procedure, which is the key's own wording; answerable without the rest of the passage.

CS-H-16.note: Checked hard per instruction. A is a strong distractor and shares the key's opening ('two rival accounts'), but it is decisively defeated by 'It has not been analyzed' - data that has not been analyzed cannot favor either account. Not second-defensible. Medium rather than hard because the defeat is a flat contradiction in the final sentence rather than a second feature that has to be weighed against the first.

CS-H-17.note: C is the strongest distractor in the cross-text set because Text 2 really does mention mortality and Text 1 really does claim a cost 'paid once' - but the stem asks about the emergency-call claim, and C answers a different claim. Correctly excluded on stem scope, which is a legitimate SAT discrimination. Key paraphrases Text 2's closing sentence.

CS-H-18.note: Key unique: A contradicts Text 2's own concession that the shells are 'the stronger find', C invents a sediment-contamination claim, D grants symbolic behavior that Text 2 withholds. Good design detail worth copying: D is a second concessive-shaped option, so the concede-and-counter form does not by itself identify the key here (unlike CS-H-19 and CS-H-21). Key restates Text 2's last sentence clause by clause.

CS-H-19.note: Text 2 states the answer in two flat sentences ('Anyone at all may read these journals. Fewer people may appear in them.') and the key is their paraphrase. The other three attribute claims Text 2 never makes. Also the only option in its set with a concessive opener ('By granting'), so the answer shape is visible before the content.

CS-H-20.note: The best cross-text item: B is genuinely attractive (task differences are the obvious methodological objection) and is refuted by Text 2's last sentence, 'The studies that find the effect and the studies that do not use the same tasks' - a distractor pre-empted on purpose. Key comes from the middle of Text 2 rather than its closing line, so the closing-sentence heuristic does not solve it.

CS-H-21.note: Key unique; the concession is carried by 'without anyone's having argued for them' in Text 2's closing clause. A is a plausible trap but is about fleet behavior, which only Text 1 discusses. Two weaknesses: the stem lifts 79 characters of Text 1 verbatim, and the key is the only concessive option in the set ('By accepting'), against denying / arguing / maintaining.

CS-H-22.note: Key is a real abstraction of Text 2's opening sentence rather than a restatement ('constrains what a clerk may write down; it does not constrain what a witness ... will say'), which is why this survives as medium. A is self-refuting since Text 2 relies on the questions having survived. Uniform 'By arguing' opener across all four options - no speech-act tell.

CS-H-23.note: Key is a near-verbatim restatement of Text 2's final sentence ('The two models that favor recovery both assume a stream of feedstock that does not exist'), so almost no inference is required. D is Text 1's own argument, which is a fair trap for a careless reader but not for a comprehending one. Stem also lifts 60 characters of Text 1's claim.

CS-H-24.note: Key restates Text 2's second sentence, but that sentence is a two-branch construction ('consistent with X ... and equally consistent with Y') that a student has to hold whole, which keeps it above easy. Distractors are all claims neither text makes. Shortest cross-text stem and the only one that does not lift a long span of Text 1.
